verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's own docs describe CKS, a managed Kubernetes service, with kubeconfig and kubectl access and Cluster Autoscaler support. They also describe SUNK, which runs Slurm jobs inside Kubernetes so batch training and services share one compute pool, sparing users from building their own scheduler. Missing for 10: detailed SUNK job-submission and scheduler-configuration documentation (only overview statements are present), and independent or hands-on corroboration of managed Slurm/Kubernetes scheduling.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes

citations.quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud.
Run training and inference workloads on the same cluster by running Slurm jobs inside Kubernetes.
With SUNK, one pool of compute serves batch training jobs through Slurm and long-running or bursty services through Kubernetes.
Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.
